subject.title: Feature: Private Mode for demos and content creation

question: What exact privacy guarantee and activation scope should OpenClaw promise for private sessions?
rationale: Source inspection establishes that the mode is absent, but code cannot choose the allowed metadata, workspace-read rules, tool and media handling, plugin indexing, channel authorization, restart-loss semantics, or activation UX.

options.title: Enforceable per-session mode
options.body: Promise no private workspace context and no durable conversation content, with explicit narrow metadata exceptions and accepted loss on restart.

options.title: Demo-only context suppression
options.body: Suppress persona and memory bootstrap files for presentations while explicitly making no no-persistence security promise.

options.title: Defer the feature
options.body: Retain current retention and deletion controls until complete cross-surface enforcement is supportable.

recommendation.title: Enforceable per-session mode
recommendation.body: Promise no private workspace context and no durable conversation content, with explicit narrow metadata exceptions and accepted loss on restart.

likelyOwner.reason: Repository history and the prior canonical review make this the strongest available owner for the security and product contract.
